scope: Original Fantasy Flight English 2008 CE01, 50 aliens; base rules and applicable official FAQ. Exclude Technology/variants, Anniversary extras and expansions.

questions.question: For a three-player standard game, how are aliens selected, which flares enter the cosmic deck, how many cards does each player receive, and how is the first player selected?
What counts as one colony, can several players have colonies on one planet, and do five foreign colonies have to be in different systems?
At the start of an encounter, must the offense retrieve a warp ship if available, and where does the original rulebook place it when the offense has colonies or has none?
What happens when destiny has only one card left, and what choices does drawing your own color offer if your home system contains a foreign colony or a completely empty planet?
Without a special power, may offense attack Blue’s foreign colony in Red’s home system after drawing Blue, and who defends Red’s empty home planet if foreign bystanders are present?
From where and how many ships may the offense launch, may it strip a colony, and can the defense move ships onto or off the targeted planet during Launch?
In what order are allies invited and committed, can someone invited by both sides join both, and where do defensive allies put their ships?
An attacking side has an attack 10 and six ships; defense has attack 12 and four ships. Who wins, and what happens to offense, offensive allies, defense, defensive allies and bystanders?
When offense wins an attack, where do ships on each side go, do existing bystander colonies survive, and does reinforcing an existing colony earn another colony?
A defensive ally contributes three ships to a winning defense. May they combine cards and warp retrieval as rewards, and where do the allied and retrieved ships go?

If a main player’s negotiate loses to attack and that player loses three ships to warp while two allied ships also go there, how much compensation is collected, from where, and what if opponent holds fewer cards?
When both reveal negotiate, what happens to allies, what may the main players exchange, where may a new colony be granted, what makes a valid deal, and what is the failure penalty/time limit?
What does Morph copy and when, does it track later changes to the opponent’s card, and what happens after the encounter?
Who may play reinforcements, when, on which side, and when is the reinforcement response window finished?
What are the ordinary per-player and per-card flare limits, when does a played flare return to hand, and when does an alien use its own Wild instead of Super?

When offense lacks encounter cards at start of turn, when defense lacks them at Planning, and when offense loses its last one later, what are the hand replacement and ship-return rules? Is playing other cards before replacement compulsory?
After a successful first encounter may offense start a second with no encounter card, hoping to obtain one later? What ends an ordinary turn after first or second encounter?
Exactly when is an ordinary alien power lost and regained for home colony count, can it be used one last time upon loss, and does a Cosmic Zap stop every printed part of the sheet?

When contradictory effects really occur simultaneously, what player order resolves them? Can a player generally interrupt a resolving effect with another non-Zap action, and may a power be preemptively Cosmic Zapped?

When are ordinary five-foreign-colony victories checked, can wins be shared, and what happens when Tick-Tock removes its last token because two main players make a deal that gives both their fifth foreign colony?

For Amoeba, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain what ship presence is required to Ooze, when relative to card selection/reveal does it happen, from/to where and how many ships may move, and can a shipless winner receive a colony?

For Anti-Matter, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain which card pairing triggers Negation, which side wins, how are own, opposing main-player and both sides' allied ships counted, and which ordinary tie rule remains?

For Barbarian, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain which result triggers Loot and Pillage, when relative to compensation, who sees/chooses how many cards, and what happens to the remaining hand?

For Calculator, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when is equalizing announced, which revealed card pairing permits it, what changes and what stays fixed, and what values result from attacks15 and8?

For Chosen, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain how often and when may Divine Intervention be used, how many cards are drawn, what happens with no encounters, what replacements/addition are allowed, and where do replaced/unused cards go?

For Citadel, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when, where and from what may citadels be placed; which portion requires power use; when/how many activate; what bonus applies; and what happens to activated/unactivated citadels after defense wins or loses?

For Clone, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when relative to outcome, compensation and discard may Replicate act, and which card does it return to where?

For Cudgel, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain what result and revealed card trigger Smash, how many extra ships must which player lose, who chooses them, and are normal losses replaced? Does successfully making a deal count as a successful encounter, as a win for Cudgel or Barbarian, or both? Cudgel originally reveals a negotiate and then uses Human Wild to turn it into attack 42. Does that transformation satisfy Cudgel's requirement to have revealed an attack?

For Dictator, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain on whose turns and when is Command used, what selection information and choice does it give, and how is destiny handled on Dictator's turn or when zapped?

For Fido, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when may Fetch act, which card is offered to whom, what happens on refusal versus acceptance, and what benefit may Fido receive?
For Filch, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when may Theft act, whose encounter card is taken from where and added to whose hand?

For Fodder, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain what pairing and timing permit Overwhelm, which hand attack values qualify relative to both revealed attacks, how many can be discarded, and how do they affect the total?

For Gambler, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when does Bluff act relative to the opponent's reveal, what is announced, what happens if unchallenged, and on challenge who loses how many ships from which locations and how is the encounter then resolved? State the printed incompatible alien.

For Grudge, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when are tokens assigned, to whom, what happens for each of Grudge's win/deal and loss/failed-deal branches, who chooses penalty ships and which ships are ineligible?

For Hacker, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when collecting compensation, from whose hand may Hack take cards and who looks/chooses them; when Hacker owes compensation, who selects what the opponent receives?

For Hate, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when does Rage act, what must Hate discard, what alternatives does each other player have, what attack threshold does the original sheet print, who selects lost ships, and what happens if Hate then lacks encounters?

For Healer, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain what event and whose losses permit Heal, how many of that event's ships return and where, what card benefit is earned, can several players be healed, and does healing remove compensation?

For Human, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when does Humanity act, what bonus does it add to which side, and what happens if this use is zapped?

For Kamikaze, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when may Sacrifice act, how many ships from where may be sacrificed, what cards result, and what happens to those ships if the use is zapped?

For Loser, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when is Upset declared, what card-selection restriction follows, how does it change the outcome and when does that reversal happen relative to other effects including zapped Human?

For Machine, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain after what outcomes may Continuity grant another encounter, how many encounters may its turn contain and what hand requirement remains?

For Macron, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain under the retained official erratum, when are Mass's launch/ally limitation and ship-strength uses made, what ship limit applies to offense/allies, how much is each ship worth for total versus compensation/rewards, and does the defense itself have the one-ship launch limit? When a Virus Wild or Super effect specifies the number of ships, does each Macron ship count as one ship or four?

For Masochist, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when exactly is Hurt Yourself checked, what lost-ship locations count, what is the alternate win condition, is it lost for too few home colonies, and can Masochist still win normally? If an in-scope alien effect explicitly causes an immediate game win, must play continue until the end of Resolution? What can interrupt that winning effect before it resolves?

For Mind, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when and whose hand may Knowledge inspect, how does being a main player restrict that target, and what may Mind reveal to other players?

For Mirror, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when is Reversal declared, which revealed cards are changed, how are digits treated, and what values result from15,20 and08?

For Miser, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain what extra hands and choice are given at setup, how may Hoard substitute for the ordinary hand, can gains be put there or opponents inspect/draw from it, and when/how can the hoard be replaced?

For Mite, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when and at what defense hand-size threshold does Bluster act, what two alternatives does defense have, how are cards discarded, and what are ship destinations and encounter status under each choice?

For Mutant, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when and at what hand size may Regenerate act, from which sources and in what sequence/randomness are cards taken, and when does drawing stop?

For Observer, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain in what roles may Protect act, whose ships are protected in each role, during what phase and from which loss destination are they returned to where?

For Oracle, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when does Foresee act, whose card is played in what manner first, and when does Oracle then select and play its own?

For Pacifist, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain which revealed pairing triggers Peace and who wins, and what happens when both reveal negotiate?

For Parasite, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when may Infest act, what invitation and side choices does it change, how many ships are sent, and can it override an effect that specifically prevents alliance?

For Philanthropist, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when may Giving act, how many cards from where go to which eligible recipient, when can that card be used, and under what own-hand/role condition is a new hand drawn?

For Reincarnator, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain what results trigger Reincarnation, where is the replacement drawn from and which candidates are rejected, what happens on later losses, what old power remains, and what happens when another power copies this one and then loses?

For Remora, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain what separate retrieval and draw events permit Cling, how much is obtained per event, where do the benefits come from, and what same-encounter retrieval restriction applies?

For Reserve, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when may Reinforce turn which attack cards into what value, how many may it use, and what cost cancels another player's reinforcement and where does that canceled card go?

For Shadow, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain which destiny draws trigger Execute, who chooses whose ship from which location, how is wild handled and must its target match offense's chosen defense?

For Sorcerer, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when relative to selection/reveal does Magic act, what is switched, and which card does each player reveal afterward?

For Spiff, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain under the retained official crash-landing erratum, what card pairing, losing margin and role permit Crash Land, how many ships escape what loss and land where, and which coexistence restrictions remain? Does the margin condition include a low-total-wins encounter?

For Tick-Tock, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain how many tokens are set up in the standard five-planet game, which two types of events remove tokens, what happens at the final token, and can Tick-Tock still win normally?

For Trader, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when may Transference act, which hands are exchanged and who keeps which hand afterward?

For Tripler, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when does Thrice act, what card type is required, what happens at values10-or-less versus above10, and what rounding applies? Calculate attacks10 and11.

For Vacuum, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain what event triggers Catharsis, how many additional ships may be lost, who chooses targets/quantities versus exact colony sources, can Vacuum target itself, and are these losses additional to ordinary losses?

For Virus, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when does Multiply act, how are its own ships and attack card combined, how are allied ships counted, and what total results from attack8, three own ships and two allied ships?

For Void, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain what result and role trigger Eradicate, whose ships go to which destination, what minimum number of surviving ships is protected in this standard game and where do excess losses go? If an opponent has six ships not permanently removed and would lose three, how many can be eradicated and how many go to warp?

For Vulch, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain whose discarded artifacts trigger Salvage, does played versus unplayed matter, can it salvage its own played artifacts, and what special reveal/retention/new-draw procedure applies when refreshing a hand?

For Warpish, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when and with which revealed card may Necromancy act, whose warp ships count, and how much do they add?

For Warrior, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain under the retained official experience erratum, in which role/results are tokens gained and in what quantities; when/how is the combat bonus used, what card type is required and are the tokens spent? If Warrior's power is Cosmic Zapped, does Warrior still gain experience from an otherwise qualifying encounter result?

For Will, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain under the official timing correction, when does Choice act, how may it change the opponent/location, what third-player-system colony requirement remains, and do other effects of the drawn destiny card still occur?

For Zombie, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain when does Immortality prevent a warp loss, where are ships sent instead, which additional deal clause does not require power use, who may be liberated under the FAQ and where do freed ships go? Is there a numerical limit on how many ships Zombie may liberate as part of a deal? May Zombie free a third player's ships, such as Masochist's, while negotiating with someone else?

A player must draw from the cosmic deck, but both it and its discard pile are empty. What procedure makes a new deck and hands? If that still cannot provide full hands, what happens to Miser's hoard and other setup card holdings?

Do Zombie ships kept out of the warp by Zombie's power and ships eradicated by Void earn negotiate compensation? Would Zombie instead qualify if its power were zapped and those ships actually reached the warp?

For base effects, distinguish ships that are losing an encounter, ships lost to the warp, and ships sent to the warp. Can a losing Zombie ship avoid becoming lost, and do ships sent by a separate effect count as lost?

Before compensation starts, may you legally play a reinforcement to remove it from your hand? Once Hacker has targeted your hand, may you then dump it, and what kinds of effects can interrupt the hand-targeting action?
When Mobius Tubes releases a player's ships and that player has no colonies, where do those ships end up? What extra placement can the offense make before remaining ships return to the warp?
Does Start Turn happen on both encounters of a turn or only the first? If the offense needs a new hand and another player wants to use a Regroup Plague, which happens first?
When discard order matters, in what order are non-encounter cards discarded, and how are the main players' encounter cards ordered so that one ends on top?

When offense automatically reclaims a completely empty home planet after drawing its own color, through which encounter phase does play proceed? Does the reclamation count as a win and a successful encounter, and does Warrior earn experience for it? How many ships may be placed on that empty home planet, and from which holdings may they come?

If you have no ships outside the encounter, may you pay a Void Wild cost that specifically requires an outside ship using an involved ship? If Grudge instead requires outside ships to be lost when none exist, how many do you lose?
If the offense cannot place a ship in the gate, or its last ship there is removed, does the encounter stop? If it wins with no ships, does that alone establish a foreign colony?
With no effect granting an exception, may a player lie about hand contents, show those cards, conceal how many cards are held, or conduct private table talk?

For encounter totals, is a modified card used at its original printed value or its current value? For an effect unrelated to encounter resolution that targets a card's identity, which identity is used, and does Morph cease to be a Morph by identity after copying an attack? Unless a specific effect says otherwise, which type/value do effects strictly determining compensation, rewards or disposition of involved ships use?
Are discard piles ordinarily public, and may other players inspect every card discarded faceup in a simultaneous group before deciding how to respond?
After losing its alien power, is a player still considered to be that alien for effects that care about alien identity?

Can Fodder or Reserve discard one attack for its power, observe the result, and then add more in another use during that Reveal phase? Can Kamikaze sacrifice and draw one ship at a time to decide how many to sacrifice?
Although defensive allies physically place ships next to the target planet, are those ships considered in the hyperspace gate for effects using that phrase?
Unless an effect says otherwise, who chooses which ships a player loses as an extra penalty, and must a chosen ship be under that player's control?
When Plague requires one card of each type held, which types exist in the original base cosmic deck? Is Morph a separate type, and is encounter an additional type?

If chosen aliens conflict because one has a printed Do Not Use restriction, which alien leaves the game? What two replacement options does the affected player have, and what happens if another conflict is drawn?
Is an encounter legal if gaining a foreign colony would necessarily require making a deal, rather than being possible without a deal?
Are alien powers universally limited to one use per encounter? What usage rule applies absent specific text, and how do Hate and Vulch illustrate explicit/context-based limits?
If another player's timely action or the timing-order result changes the state after you announce an optional power/effect, may you change your mind about invoking it?

When granting a deal colony, must you vacate your own colony? Can a valid deal be one-sided? Can future promises be added and enforced, and may a player lie about explicit card terms in the agreed deal?

If a flare itself is Card Zapped, does the attempted play use that player's one-flare allowance? Compare a flare prevented by Anti-Matter: does it stay in hand, use the allowance, or become available to attempt again later that encounter?

Your power is zapped, so you use your own alien's Wild flare. Its text would normally give the flare to that alien or discard it if that alien is absent. Do you keep it, give it away, or discard it after resolution?
If a Super flare lets an alien use its power as an ally or in a phase outside the sheet's ordinary highlighted phases, can the actual power use still be Cosmic Zapped in either case?

A player has already played its Super flare, and the power use enabled by it is Cosmic Zapped. Must the flare be discarded or its Wild used immediately? While the power is zapped, which effect would apply to a legal flare play, and does the zap permit that already-played flare to be played a second time in the same encounter?

May you wait to see Chosen's divine-intervention cards or the card Philanthropist gives before deciding to Cosmic Zap that power? If you pass and later reinforcements change the winner, or play moves into the next phase, may you then retroactively Zap that earlier use?
If an alien is Cosmic Zapped during Start Turn, does its power return for Regroup or another later phase of that same encounter?

Amoeba legally invokes ooze to move all twenty ships, which will reduce its home colonies below the power-maintenance threshold. Does loss of its power interrupt the move, or when does the loss occur?

A player initially joins Grudge with at least one ship, then all its allied ships leave through Amoeba Super or Force Field. Does the player still count as having allied, and does it receive a Grudge token for that encounter?
May Amoeba Wild increase a player's ship count when that player is defending with zero ships?

After being played once, do Anti-Matter Super, Cudgel Super, Kamikaze Super, Machine Super, Masochist Super, Miser Super, or Machine Wild automatically apply in later encounters, or must the corresponding flare be played again each encounter its effect is desired?
Is Chosen's Super flare played before Chosen looks at its divine-intervention cards, or after inspecting them?
What happens to existing citadels when Citadel's sheet is turned facedown through power loss, and what happens if that sheet is discarded?
After Sorcerer switches the encounter cards, which final card does Clone keep and which does Filch take?
If Clone, Filch and Fido all have possible claims on played encounter cards, does Clone keep its card before the others act, and how is priority between Filch and Fido decided?

When Clone Super permits up to double normal compensation, must Clone choose exactly normal or exactly double, or may it choose an intermediate amount? Must the opponent have sufficient cards for the chosen compensation amount?
Does Mind's ability to inspect another player's hand also permit inspection of Miser's hoard?
Can Fido retrieve encounter cards discarded to Plague, Fodder or Reserve during the encounter, or only the encounter cards actually played as such?
Can Filch take Gambler's encounter card when Gambler never reveals it, and where is that card placed instead of being discarded?
If only one side invited you this encounter, does Fodder Wild let you join the other side anyway?
For Fodder Super, must discarded attacks be lower than Fodder's own attack, lower than the opponent's, or can they be above the opponent's?
When Gambler faces Oracle, must Gambler reveal or bluff before Oracle chooses its encounter card, or may Gambler wait for Oracle's choice?

May Hate discard Morph, and what must the others then discard to avoid losing ships? If Hate uses an attack, may someone discard a lower attack despite still taking the loss? Does Hate draw a needed new offensive hand before using its power, and what happens to its selected discard if the power is zapped?

Does Healer prevent ships reaching the warp or retrieve them after they arrive, and can that retrieval trigger Remora? Can Healer heal ordinary Zombie prevention? If it heals Vacuum, has Vacuum already been able to take other ships, and may those non-Healer victims also be healed?
If Human's zapped-power win and Pacifist's negotiate win conflict in one encounter, what decides which victory effect controls?

Can Human be zapped to win when one or both main players revealed negotiate? If its opponent revealed negotiate, when does that opponent receive compensation after Human's win? May Human play Cosmic Zap on its own power use?
With Human Super, may Human add eight and then discard the flare to zap itself? May it instead discard solely to zap without taking the plus eight?
When Machine Wild guarantees a second encounter but the player needs a new hand to take it, what happens to the old hand and to the Machine flare during the replacement?
What changes if Macron is Cosmic Zapped while launching versus after encounter cards are revealed? Does Macron Super's permission to launch up to four ships include being a defensive ally?

For Mind Wild, Reserve Wild and Vulch Super, must the flare be replayed for each later qualifying event in that encounter, or does one play last through the encounter? When is Vulch Super first played, and may Vulch collect that same Super through its effect? While Reserve Wild remains active, whose discarded cards of what type may its user take, and where do those cards go?

When a card played from Miser's hoard returns, which holding receives it? If only the hoard has an encounter card, may Miser start a second encounter? Can Miser use the hoard to satisfy a required hand discard such as Hate?
May a player using Miser Wild save fewer than two cards?

While allied during Resolution, can Observer lose ships outside the encounter to Grudge, and may it relocate the protected ships instead? May it use Void Wild without losing its ship cost? Does this protection also apply in phases before Resolution?
When Loser calls an upset and Pacifist must play negotiate, does Pacifist receive compensation if Loser revealed attack? What if Loser did not reveal attack?
Can the defense invoke the ordinary timing priority to avoid playing the card given by Philanthropist Super?
If Philanthropist Wild lends Miser's power, does Miser's hoard travel with the lent power?

When does Reincarnator Wild take effect, and can a target use its power earlier in the encounter even in the same nominal phase? May the Wild target its own player? Can Reincarnator use the Super flares of its temporary incarnations?
If Reserve is Cosmic Zapped just as it is about to play an attack as reinforcement, is that attack discarded or kept?
If multiple destiny cards are drawn during one Destiny phase, does Shadow execute for each drawn card or only for the final card used?
Can Trader become defense with an empty hand and trade that empty hand to offense, or must it draw before trading?

May Vacuum target itself to create another loss? If one Vacuum Super effect removes ships from several single-ship Zombie colonies at once, can Zombie save a ship to another colony that the same effect is also removing?
If Virus Wild is used without any allies, is the relevant multiplier zero?
Does a failed deal with Void eradicate ships? When Void wins as a main player, or as an ally using its Super, can it eradicate? Do Zombie or Observer prevent that eradication?
Can Vulch retrieve the Cosmic Zap that just zapped its power? If another player using Vulch Wild discards artifacts, can an active Vulch retrieve them even if it then has to hand them back again?
If ships enter the warp during Reveal, does Warpish always update its encounter total? How does arrival before Warpish uses its power differ from arrival afterward?
May Zombie use Kamikaze Wild or a similar card requiring its ships to be sent to the warp, and then use Zombie's power to keep those ships from entering the warp?
In the FAQ's specifically named case of a player with no colonies or ships on their own turn, what ship is retrieved during Regroup and where may it be placed?

Hacker is the offense and will collect compensation from another player who is a successful defensive ally. With that ally about to draw ordinary cosmic-deck rewards, does Hacker's compensation resolve before or after those rewards under the timing rules?

A player strips their last ship from a colony to join an encounter. Afterward, may their returning or warp-retrieved ships restore that now-empty location without a specific exception? If a required relocation has no existing colony anywhere to receive the ships, where do they go?

Under the original rulebook, a special destiny card designates the offense itself as the defense. May that player instead try to drive out a foreign colony in their own system; how is the actual defending colony chosen and what happens to other colors there?

Oracle and Sorcerer are the main players. Explain their complete card-selection and swapping sequence, including which card is faceup or facedown at each step and whether their sharing a Planning phase makes the effects simultaneous.
When using Clone Wild, what happens to an artifact you play, may it be played again during the same encounter merely because it was retained, and what printed role/phase applies to the flare?

Using the classic Filch Wild flare, what items may you illicitly take and from which locations, where may the retrieved ships go, when must the flare be revealed and when may it be zapped, what happens if caught, and what changes about the deck/discards after it is revealed? Under its printed role and phase permissions, may an uninvolved player perform the classic Filch Wild cheating action during another player's Regroup?
For the original classic Filch Super shown in the rulebook, which player role and phase are printed, whose used encounter card may be filched, and must the user have participated in that encounter?

Under the retained official Mind Wild erratum, when can the flare be played, which later draws does that one play intercept, what does the user do with each intercepted card, and may the information be shared?

Under the retained Reincarnator Wild erratum, what event and target restrictions permit giving the flare to another player, when does that target replace its power, and which replacement aliens are rejected?

Before choosing aliens, how are the warp, player planets, ships and colony markers set up in a standard game, which destiny cards are removed or retained, and may both Filch flare versions be included?

In an ordinary encounter, what opponent and system choices does a wild destiny card permit, how does a special destiny card determine the defense and location, what color does a special count as for color-sensitive effects, and do hazard symbols change base play?

May the two main players invite one another as allies? Without an exception, may an uninvited other player join, may an invitee refuse, and how many ships from where does each joining ally commit? After alliances, which players select encounter cards, which types are legal, how are they placed/revealed, and when are they normally discarded?
Can an artifact be selected as the encounter card, how do you determine when and how it may be played, and what is its normal destination after play?

When a deal grants a colony, must the recipient use only its ships on the hyperspace gate or may it use other ships, and which ship location is excluded? After the deal, where do any remaining offensive gate ships return?

A defensive ally has three defender rewards. May it draw a card, inspect it and then decide whether the remaining rewards will be more cards or warp ships? When must it commit to the full mix of reward sources?
When Mobius Tubes releases a player's ships and those ships are placed on that player's existing colonies, do the ships land simultaneously or one ship at a time?
Without a specific card or alien exception, do you draw a card or new hand merely because an encounter ends, a turn ends, or your hand becomes empty?

During an ordinary Launch after destiny specifies the system, who chooses the target planet within that system, and where are the offense's launched ships placed? During Alliance, where does a joining offensive ally place its committed ships?
Without a special exception, how many defender rewards does a successful defensive ally receive for its contributed ships, and may it choose to skip those rewards?
Under the original rulebook, name the seven phases of an ordinary encounter in order. How is the separate Start Turn step related to this sequence on the first encounter?
In an ordinary attack-versus-attack encounter, what does a legally played reinforcement card do to the total of the side it is played on?

For the FAQ-quoted Mite Super instruction to take any cards its opponent discards, is pickup restricted to encounter cards, or can it include another original-base card type such as a discarded artifact?

In the official FAQ Oracle Wild example, are the hands kept separate or mixed together, is the new hand chosen selectively or at random, and where is the Oracle flare during that process and afterward?
For a legally played Loser Wild flare, must it be played before encounter cards are selected, or can it first be played after selection?
Must a player be a main player or an ally to play Cosmic Zap on an alien's power use, or may a bystander play it?
